title: Lasers; Diagnostic X-ray production and detection; Wave–particle duality; Doppler effect; Expanding universe and cosmology
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: X-XRAY-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; X-XRAY-2#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: A03-1#N.4, A03-2#N.3, Q03-1#N.4a, W11-1#N.12b, A03-1#N.6, A03-2#N.7, Q03-1#N.17b, W11-1#N.13c, A03-1#N.8, A03-2#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Thermionic emission
items.clue: Release of electrons from the hot filament of the cathode.

items.label: de Broglie wavelength
items.clue: The quantity h/p for any moving object; it gets shorter as momentum rises.

items.label: Electron gun
items.clue: Hot filament plus an accelerating potential of a few kV, producing the beam.

items.label: Intensifying screen
items.clue: Placed in front of film in a conventional detector to turn X-rays into light.

questions.stem: A galaxy recedes from the Earth at 1.5 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. A line in its spectrum has a laboratory wavelength of 486.1 nm. At what wavelength is the line observed?
A galaxy at a distance of 1.2 × 10²⁴ m recedes from the Earth at 2800 km s⁻¹. What value of the Hubble constant does this give?
questions.explanation: H₀ = speed ÷ distance = 2.8 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ ÷ 1.2 × 10²⁴ m = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹.

questions.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?
A source of sound of frequency 500 Hz moves directly towards a stationary observer at 20 m s⁻¹. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. What wavelength does the observer receive?
questions.explanation: In one period the source moves 0.040 m closer, so λ′ = (340 − 20)/500 = 0.64 m.

questions.stem: Andromeda, our nearest large neighbour galaxy, shows a blue shift. Does this contradict the expansion of the universe?

options.text: Yes: in an expanding universe, every galaxy must be moving away from us.
No: space is contracting in our part of the universe, drawing Andromeda in.
No: its light looks blue because Andromeda contains many hot, blue stars.
No: at so short a distance, its own motion towards us outweighs expansion.

questions.explanation: Cosmological red shift is tiny over so short a journey. Andromeda's motion through space towards us gives a larger Doppler blue shift.

questions.stem: A measured value of the Hubble constant is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. What is the estimated age of the universe? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)
A beam of electrons and a beam of protons are each accelerated from rest through 100 V and aimed at the same crystal, whose rows of atoms are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Which beam shows clear diffraction?

options.text: Only the protons: they are heavier, so they hit the atoms harder and are scattered more.
Both equally: they have the same charge and the same p.d., so they gain the same energy.
Only the electrons: their wavelength is comparable with the spacing of the atoms.
Neither: diffraction is a property of waves, and both beams are made of particles.

questions.stem: A train sounds a 400 Hz horn as it moves directly away from a stationary listener. The listener receives a wavelength of 0.925 m. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How fast is the train moving?

options.text: 30 m s⁻¹, but towards the listener

questions.explanation: Behind a receding source λ′ = (v + u_s)/f, so u_s = λ′f − v = 0.925 × 400 − 340 = 30 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A hydrogen absorption line has a laboratory wavelength of 656.28 nm. In the spectrum of a star in our own galaxy, it is observed at 656.08 nm. What is the star's velocity along the line of sight?

options.text: 9.1 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ away from the Earth

questions.stem: Galaxy P is 2.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 5.2 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Galaxy Q is 6.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 1.56 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Assuming each has always moved at its present speed, how long ago was each at our position? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

options.text: P 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago, Q 3.7 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they set off at different times.
Both 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Both 3.8 × 10¹⁷ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Never: the further galaxy moves faster, so the two can never have been together.

questions.explanation: Distance ÷ speed = 3.8 × 10¹⁷ s for both, which is 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years. Speed ∝ distance gives every galaxy the same time.
